copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Survives a Dead Receiving Corps
copies.body:
CJ started two wide receivers and got two points. Rashee Rice posted a zero on a 14.9 projection, Parker Washington managed 2.0 on 15.3, and CJ still won, because Jonathan Taylor (22.7), Chuba Hubbard (25.9) and Quinshon Judkins (21.6) combined for 70.2 out of the backfield. The running backs beat Noah's by 13.9, the flex added another 5.1, and that was the entire margin plus change. Everything else on the board belonged to Noah.
Noah's problem was the same one, from the other direction. Garrett Wilson (5.7 on 16.5) and Josh Downs (4.6 on 13.6) cost him roughly 20 points of expectation, and Drake Maye sat on the bench with 26.2 while Patrick Mahomes gave him 17.0. Flip that one lineup call and Noah is 1-3 instead of staring at an 0-4 with a 7-37 all-play, worst in the league by a wide margin.
We had CJ by 19 and he found a harder way to get there. CJ is 3-1 but ranks 6th in scoring with luck running +0.8 — borrowed time. Noah, the man nobody drafts against in November, is currently the worst team in the league by every available measure.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Backfield Buries Grant Despite Goose Egg
copies.body:
The running backs decided this one and it wasn't subtle. Ashton Jeanty and RJ Harvey combined for 37.9, nearly doubling the 20.3 Grant got from Omarion Hampton and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, and Jared Goff tacked on another nine-point edge over Kyler Murray, who came in 7.7 under projection. Grant's receivers actually won the day — Zay Flowers 25.8, Amon-Ra St. Brown 15.5 — and he still lost by 5.2, which is what happens when your QB and both backs quietly underdeliver at once.
Kaleb should not have been able to absorb a zero from Ladd McConkey, who didn't play. Carnell Tate put up 21.5 on his bench. That's a 21.5-point margin of error he never needed, because Grant was busy leaving Jaylen Waddle (14.5) and Tony Pollard (13.0) stapled down behind Christian Watson and Croskey-Merritt.
We picked Grant by nine, which aged about as well as the Watson start. He's 2-2 with a 36% all-play, 10th in the league — the record is generous. Kaleb's 3-1 on +1.1 luck wins, which is its own kind of generous, but a win's a win and he's been here before.

copies.headline: Kincaid Sinks Isaac While Hockenson Watches
copies.body:
Isaac lost this at tight end and kicker, which is a humiliating sentence to write. Dalton Kincaid put up 1.7 on a 10.7 projection while T.J. Hockenson scored 24.9 on Isaac's bench — a 23-point swing by itself, in a 25.4-point game. Add Chris Boswell's 3.1 against Cam Little's 14.7 and the two spots nobody thinks about accounted for the entire margin. Javonte Williams' 31.3 and Malik Nabers' 23.2 were more than enough firepower. The lineup card wasn't.
John didn't need to be sharp. Matthew Stafford managed 9.7, Trey McBride came in 7.3 under, D'Andre Swift was invisible, and he still cleared 135 because Kyren Williams went for 36.7 and Puka Nacua added 27.7. Our preview had John by 11; he doubled it without his quarterback showing up.
Both sit 2-2, but the underlying numbers aren't close — John is 26-18 in all-play, Isaac 13-31 and still somehow above .500. One of these records is real.

copies.headline: Adam's Running Backs Bury Mitchell Again
copies.body:
The backfield did it. Kenneth Walker III went for 30.9 and Adam's running backs cleared Mitchell's by 16.3, which was already more than Mitchell could spare. Then Sam LaPorta's 22.4 doubled Tyler Warren, and Will Reichard — a kicker — outscored Mitchell's entire tight end and defense allotment by himself at 20.0. Three positions, roughly 41 points of edge, and the Jets D/ST contributed a clean zero without ever mattering.
Mitchell actually won the receiver room, mostly on Nico Collins at 30.8, but got almost nothing else. Jahmyr Gibbs missed his 26.1 projection by 8.4, George Holani turned 10.3 into 3.0, and DJ Moore posted 2.7 against a 13.0 projection. That's three starters torching a week at once. We picked Adam by 21 and were conservative.
Mitchell falls to 1-3 with a 43% all-play, so the bad luck story is thinner than he'd like. Adam is 4-0, 40-4 in all-play, and leading the league in scoring. Quietly relentless, as advertised.

copies.headline: Peter's Receivers Erase Leif In One Afternoon
copies.body:
The wideouts did it, and it wasn't close. Peter got 50.5 from Tee Higgins and Romeo Doubs; Leif got 15.7 out of Davante Adams and Stefon Diggs combined, with Adams turning a 15.6 projection into 7.2. Add Kyle Monangai's 28.0 and Bijan Robinson's 27.7 against a quiet 31.9 from Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry, and the running back gap alone was 23.8. Lamar Jackson beat Josh Allen by four tenths of a point. That was the only fair fight on the board.
Leif's whole roster quit at once. Dalton Schultz managed 2.9 on a 9.0 projection, David Montgomery gave back 4.3 on 13.5 while Mike Evans sat on 12.6, and 82.8 is his season low by nearly 40. We picked Leif by 16, which looks adorable now.
Peter is 4-0 with his season high, though the all-play says 27-17 and luck says +1.5 wins — he's been good, not this good. Leif falls to 2-2 and back toward the basement he decorates so well.

copies.headline: Logan's Backfield Produced 8.5 Points. Game Over.
copies.body:
The receivers canceled out — Tetairoa McMillan went for 45.2, CeeDee Lamb answered with 41.3, and the two WR rooms finished within a point of each other. This was decided in the backfield, where Chase Brown and Aaron Jones Sr. combined for 35.9 and Logan's running backs mustered 8.5. Saquon Barkley put up 2.0 against a 14.3 projection, Jeremiyah Love managed 6.5 on 15.6, and the kicker spot added insult: Brandon Aubrey 10.9, Chase McLaughlin 2.0. That's 36.3 points of margin from two positions nobody was worried about.
The bench was worse than the start. Emanuel Wilson scored 27.0 in Logan's pocket while Barkley was busy doing nothing. Christian had his own ghosts — Alvin Kamara 22.8 on the bench behind Bhayshul Tuten's 11.1 — but when you win by 44.6 nobody audits the flex.
Christian's 157.5 is a season high and he's still 1-3, which the all-play (29-15, 2nd) says is theft. Logan is 0-4 and measuring for the dress again.

intro: Peter hung 162.98 on Leif, who managed 82.82 — an 80-point gap that qualifies less as a matchup than as a wellness check. Christian's 157.48 and Adam's 146.76 produced similar blowouts, leaving CJ's four-point escape over Noah and Kaleb's five-point win over Grant as the only two games anyone had to watch past the early window. Four of six decided by 25 or more, which makes the two coin flips feel even more unfair to the losers.
